extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and organizations applying to the DoD FY25 MURI (ONR/AFOSR/ARO) funding opportunity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for preparing and submitting White Papers and full proposals to the DoD MURI FY25 solicitation, including administrative, compliance, and technical-review standards. Covers Grants.gov/FedConnect submission steps, programmatic review criteria, and pre-award regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covered foreign country definition
rubrics_metrics.description: COVERED FOREIGN COUNTRY means the People’s Republic of China.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory electronic submission via Grants.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: All Applicants shall submit their applications online through Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White Papers must NOT be submitted through the Grants.gov application process (White papers to ONR must be submitted through FedConnect).

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM registration requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations must have an active System for Award Management (SAM) registration to apply through Grants.gov; SAM registration must be renewed annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAM registrations may take up to 7-10 days, so allow sufficient time for registration to avoid impacting application deadlines. Detailed instructions: https://www.grants.gov/applicants/applicant-registration

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov account and organizational profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must create a Grants.gov account and add a profile corresponding to the Applicant organization (enter the UEI number when adding an organizational profile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an individual is eligible, begin with creating a Grants.gov account. See Grants.gov instructions on creating profiles and eBiz POC authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: EBiz POC authorization and AOR role
rubrics_metrics.description: After creating an Organization Applicant Profile, the organization Applicant's request for Grants.gov roles is sent to the EBiz POC who must authorize roles such as the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will be able to submit once assigned the AOR role. Track role status at Grants.gov; ensure EBiz POC authorizes individuals who can make legally binding commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic signature via AOR
rubrics_metrics.description: When applications are submitted through Grants.gov, the name of the organization's AOR that submitted the application is inserted into the signature line, serving as the electronic signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EBiz POC must authorize individuals who can make legally binding commitments as AORs; failure to authorize a proper AOR is a common cause of invalid/timely submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format for attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: All attachments to grant applications submitted through Grants.gov must be in Adobe Portable Document Format (PDF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals with attachments submitted in any format other than PDF (e.g., Word, Excel) will not be considered for award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov Workspace usage and workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may use Grants.gov Workspace to create, edit, and submit application packages; Workspace allows multiple participants and progress tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a Workspace, add participants, complete required forms, check for errors, and use context-sensitive help. You may download individual PDF forms from Workspace if not using web forms. Complete SF-424 fields first to populate common fields across forms. Mandatory fields are marked with an asterisk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended early submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants.gov recommends submitting your application package at least 24-48 hours prior to the close date; DoD strongly recommends submission no later than two (2) business days ahead of the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time to correct potential technical issues; call Grants.gov Support and obtain a ticket number if experiencing submission difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of timely submission / deadline adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications must be received by 5:00 PM Eastern Time on [due date]. Proof of timely submission is the electronic date/time stamp generated by Grants.gov when the application is successfully received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications received by Grants.gov after the established due date will be considered late and not considered for funding. When DoD retrieves and acknowledges download, Grants.gov sends an additional acknowledgment; retain all confirmation emails and the tracking number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov submission acknowledgements and statuses
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission the AOR receives: (1) a submission confirmation page (receipt), (2) a Grants.gov validation receipt within two days if valid (or rejection if invalid), and (3) a DoD acknowledgment email within ten days after the due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Grants.gov Tracking Number to track status; a 'Validated' status indicates successful transmission and basic checks (virus scan, opportunity open, UEI/login match). If 'Rejected', resubmit after resolving issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic research requirement for MURI
rubrics_metrics.description: The MURI Program is funded by a basic research appropriation; White papers and proposals must be basic research rather than applied or advanced technological in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic research is defined as 'scientific study and experimentation directed toward increasing fundamental knowledge and understanding'; applied research focuses on development of useful materials/devices/systems or prototype improvement. See DoD 7000.14-R definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper evaluation focus
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers will be evaluated primarily on scientific and technical merits, potential to significantly advance fundamental understanding in the topic area, and potential DoD interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White paper assessments are used to decide whether to encourage full proposal submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal technical evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals will be evaluated on: scientific and technical merits of the proposed basic science/engineering research; potential to significantly advance fundamental understanding; potential DoD relevance and contribution to the DoD mission; qualifications and availability of the PI and investigators; adequacy of current or planned facilities and equipment to accomplish the research objectives; impact of interactions with other organizations engaged in related R&D (esp. DoD labs, industry, other defense performers); realism and reasonableness of cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost sharing is not a factor in the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism and reasonableness of cost
rubrics_metrics.description: One evaluation factor is whether proposed costs are realistic and reasonable for the work proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost proposals are evaluated by Government business professionals separately from technical review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection process responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The ultimate recommendation for award is made by the DoD scientific/technical community; recommended proposals are forwarded to Contracts and Grant Awards Management for cost analysis, responsibility determination, availability of funds, and other pre-award steps. Award is not guaranteed until the Government Grants Officer signs the award document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification of selection does not authorize spending; award documents are official instruments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of contract/grant options
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government will evaluate options for award by adding total cost for all options to the basic requirement; evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise those options during performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Government reserves the right to exercise options at time of award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation panel composition and use of external consultants
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers may be reviewed by the Research Topic Chief alone or by an evaluation panel chaired by the Research Topic Chief; panels consist of Government technical experts or IPA detailees; restrictive notices notwithstanding, support contractors or external advisors may serve as subject-matter-expert technical consultants after signing conflict-of-interest statements and NDAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support contractors/advisors with access to proposal materials must sign NDA and COI statements; selection and award decisions remain the sole responsibility of Government personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-stage evaluation procedure: technical then cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals undergo multi-stage evaluation: Government scientific experts evaluate technical proposals first; Government business professionals evaluate cost proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings are forwarded to senior DoD officials who make funding recommendations. External support contractors may be used but cannot make selection/award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial selection and proposal adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation panels and reviewing officials may recommend funding less than an entire MURI proposal (e.g., due to insufficient funds, research overlap, or potential synergies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases, proposal adjustments will be agreed to by the PI and the Government prior to final award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient qualification standards (32 CFR 22.415)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be qualified, a potential recipient must: (i) have management capability and adequate financial and technical resources to execute the proposed program given expected award funding; (ii) have a satisfactory record of executing such programs (if previously a recipient); (iii) have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics; and (iv) be otherwise qualified and eligible under applicable laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants Officers determine recipient qualifications prior to award; Applicants should provide information to assist this evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAPIIS (integrity/performance) reporting and consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: For Federal awards with total Federal share greater than the simplified acquisition threshold, the Federal awarding agency will review and consider information about the Applicant contained in the designated integrity and performance system accessible through SAM (currently FAPIIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may review and comment on entries about themselves in FAPIIS; the agency will consider applicant comments in making judgments about integrity, business ethics, and performance risk (see 2 CFR 200.205 and 41 U.S.C. 2313).

rubrics_metrics.name: Export control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are responsible for ensuring compliance with all U.S. export control laws and regulations, including ITAR (22 CFR Parts 120-130) and EAR (15 CFR Parts 730-774), as applicable. In some cases development items funded by DoD may be on the USML or CCL and subject to ITAR/EAR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should address in their proposals whether ITAR or EAR restrictions apply and are responsible for obtaining any required licenses, exemptions, or approvals for exports of hardware, technical data, software (including deemed exports), or technical assistance. ITAR/EAR references and export control reform information are provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animals — documentation prior to award
rubrics_metrics.description: If animals will be utilized, the Applicant must submit a Full Appendix or Abbreviated Appendix with supporting documentation (e.g., IACUC approval, IACUC approved protocol, most recent USDA Inspection Report) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DoD Instruction 3216.01 and DHA-MSR 6025.02. Contact the DoD Agency’s Animal Use Administrator for assistance; provide documents prior to award to permit review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of human subjects — compliance and required documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must protect rights/welfare of human subjects and comply with the Common Rule (32 CFR part 219, DoD implementation) and DoD Instruction 3216.02; for proposals involving human subjects the Applicant must submit IRB approval documents, proof of completed human research training, and the institution’s DHHS-issued Federal Wide Assurance (FWA#) prior to award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claiming exemptions under 32 CFR 219.104, include the exemption category and supporting documentation plus a short rationale signed by IRB Chair/vice Chair or designated official. If determining no human subjects research, provide supporting documentation signed by IRB leadership. Documentation must be submitted to the DoD Agency HRPO via the Program Officer. HRPO has final judgment; research cannot commence until HRPO approves the assurance and accepts IRB approval/determinations. Government will not reimburse work performed in violation (see DFARS 252.235-7004).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosafety and biosecurity compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must comply with applicable provisions of DODM 6055.18 (Safety Standards for Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories) and at least the minimum applicable requirements of CDC's BMBL and NIH Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research involving recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules (rDNA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not begin performance of research within the scope of the NIH Guidelines until receiving notice from the Contracting or Grants Officer that ONR has reviewed and accepted the Applicant’s documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide (1) a written institutional statement of compliance with NIH Guidelines (on letterhead by an institutional official other than the PI); and (2) evidence of IBC approval and DHHS Letter of Approval of the IBC or most recent DHHS compliance letter. Contact ONR HRPO for assistance involving countries outside the U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Dual Use Research of Concern (DURC) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions and USG funding agencies subject to the USG Policy for Institutional Oversight of Life Sciences Dual Use Research of Concern must comply with all listed requirements if proposals directly involve certain biological agents or toxins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the cognizant Technical Point of Contact for proposals involving such agents. Refer to U.S. Government S3 (Science, Safety, Security) guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: DoD High Performance Computing Program (HPCMP) access
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees of ONR grants and other assistance instruments may be eligible to use HPCMP assets if ONR Program Officer approval is obtained and security/screening requirements are favorably completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional information and application available at https://www.hpc.mil/.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project and Program Review Meeting expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Review Meetings between DoD sponsor and performer may be held as necessary; typically two in-person Project Review Meetings each year (approx. one day) and Program Review Meetings once per year lasting two to three days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should budget for two in-person meetings. Additional meetings may occur via teleconference or web tools. In FY24 and beyond, review meetings may be local to the funding DoD Agency or other facilities within the continental U.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional facility-hosting language for Program Review Meetings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may offer their facilities for DoD Program Review Meetings by including specified language in proposals; including or omitting this term will not affect selection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested language clarifies meetings will discuss only contracted fundamental research, no fee will be charged attendees, and the institution understands it will not be asked to host more than once per year. If a contract is awarded, facility use will be included as an option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act (FFATA) reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entities applying for financial assistance must provide information in their proposal describing necessary processes and systems to comply with reporting requirements on subawards and executive total compensation as codified in 2 CFR Part 170 Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities are required to meet reporting requirements unless an exception or exemption applies; refer to 2 CFR Part 170 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial assistance certifications and lobbying disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit certifications (e.g., SF-LLL Disclosure Form to Report Lobbying if applicable) and other required documentation as part of the Federal Assistance Certifications Report. By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 applicants certify compliance with Lobbying Disclosure Act requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If grant amount exceeds $100,000 you certify you do not have lobbying activity to disclose; if you do, attach completed SF-LLL. Instructions available at OMB/SF-LLL guidance link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpaid delinquent federal tax liability and felony conviction representation
rubrics_metrics.description: By checking 'I Agree' on SF-424 (R&R) block 17 you represent that you are not a corporation with unpaid Federal tax liability (as defined) and not a corporation convicted of a felony under any Federal law within the preceding 24 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you cannot make this representation, you are ineligible to receive an award unless a suspension and debarment official (SDO) determines further action not required to protect Government interests; applicants should promptly provide SDO information to facilitate consideration prior to award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications regarding restrictions on lobbying for awards over $100,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant awards greater than $100,000 require a certification of compliance concerning lobbying; Applicants shall provide this certification electronically via SF-424 (R&R) Block 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification applies to each grant seeking federal assistance funds exceeding $100,000; where required attach SF-LLL Disclosure of Lobbying Activities per DoD implementation (32 CFR Part 2).
